terms.note: A common PC power and board form-factor specification; it must not be assumed for proprietary server connectors.
Firmware that initializes hardware and participates in platform startup.
A controller used for out-of-band platform management and sensor access.
The server processor.
A protocol used to provide hosts with network configuration.
A removable memory module form factor.
Memory error-detection and correction information; correction limits and reporting vary by platform.
A network control protocol used by ping for Echo requests and replies.
The network-layer protocol family used for addressed packet delivery.
A platform-management interface used for sensors, events, and controller access.
The version 4 Internet Protocol address and packet format.
A storage protocol for nonvolatile memory, commonly transported over PCIe.
A computer expansion-bus family.
The serial expansion interconnect used by many server adapters and NVMe devices.
Firmware initialization and startup checks performed after power-on.
A module that converts input power into the outputs required by the server.
A storage arrangement that combines devices for performance, redundancy, or both, depending on level.
A rotational-speed unit used for fan telemetry.
A drive-health reporting system whose attributes and thresholds can be vendor-specific.
A platform firmware interface that defines boot management and other services.
